title: Rainy Halloween forecast forces cancellations and changes to Valley events - ABC30 Fresno

 Rainy Halloween forecast forces cancellations and changes to Valley events 
 By Ana Torrea Saturday, October 31, 2026 6:21AM 
 A rainy Halloween forecast is forcing some Central California communities and event organizers to cancel activities or adjust plans as wet weather moves into the region. FRESNO COUNTY, Calif. (KFSN) -- A rainy Halloween forecast is forcing some Central California communities and event organizers to cancel activities or adjust plans as wet weather moves into the region.
 While a Candy Crawl is still expected to take place Saturday in Fresno's Tower District, organizers are making adjustments to accommodate the forecast. Other events have not been as fortunate.
 In Reedley, the city announced on social media that the Halloween Harvest event has been canceled because of the expected rain.
 The event was planned in partnership with the California Fresh Farmers Market Association as part of the city's farmers market season.
 "This would've been our fourth farmers market event of the season but we had to cancel it due to the inclement weather," said Rodney Horton, the Community Development Director for the City of Reedley.
 RELATED: Rain in the forecast won't stop Halloween celebrations across the Valley 
 Horton said the farmers market has become a growing community event, but safety concerns for families and vendors prompted the decision to cancel.
 "With inclement weather comes the potential for roadway accidents and nasty spills. You know the sidewalks and streets have been dry for a period of time. So when you get that first splash of rain it could be pretty slippery," Horton said.

 Meanwhile, in Sanger, Hobbs Grove Halloween Haunt moved its activities up by a day to avoid the wet weather.
 "We don't care about rain, we love it. But you normies, you do," said entertainer 'Slappy Da Clown' of Hobbs Grove.
 "Why couldn't Mother Nature wait one more day? Just one more day. But that gives people who were going to be trick-or-treating tomorrow night, they can come out tonight," said 'Billy Bob Hobb' of Hobbs Grove.
 Despite the weather, Halloween festivities are expected to continue across the region. Law enforcement agencies also are preparing for the holiday, with the California Highway Patrol focusing on traffic safety and enforcement against impaired driving.
 The CHP is urging drivers to slow down and remain alert as rain is expected to create slick roads and hazardous driving conditions throughout Halloween night.
